reader.requirement: In a paren-free sequence of relation conditions joined by AND/OR, a relation other than the first may omit its subject, or its subject and relational operator, and is then evaluated as if the last stated subject and the last stated relational operator were inserted; the insertion stops at a complete simple condition that is not a relation; a NOT followed by GREATER, >, LESS, <, EQUAL or = is part of the operator, any other NOT is the logical operator and the operator carried is the stated one; the expanded result must satisfy Table 1.

reader.notes: All semantic probes match the 1985 expansions, and the one 85-only arm (NOT before IS is logical) prints the 1985 answer. abr4 'A = B OR (D)' is accepted at 85 and 2023 alike as A = (D), the parenthesized D being an arithmetic-expression object; the lead-in's 'no parentheses' condition is read as logical grouping, so this is judged legal, not an under-rejection. Diagnostics cite §2023 at --std 85 (wording only).

refuter.evidence: Read §1985:VI.6.3.3 whole (lead-in, SR1/SR2, insertion and termination, the NOT interpretation, the five examples) and §1985:VI.6.3.2.3 Table 1. Probes at --std 85 aimed at operators and terminators the reader did not try: a1 with A=5 B=1 C=9 D=5 K=3 (88 KC VALUE 3) printed exactly the 1985 expansions: 'A > B AND NOT >= C' 1 T (>= is not in the NOT list, so NOT is logical: 1985 has >=); 'A = B OR KC' 2 T (a condition-name stays a condition, not an object); 'A NOT = B AND NOT D' 3 T (NOT = carried, second NOT logical); 'A >= B AND <= C' 4 T; 'A < B OR NOT C' 5 F; 'A > B AND NOT LESS C' 6 F (NOT LESS operator); 'A LESS THAN OR EQUAL TO C AND B' 7 F (the 1985 compound operator carried); 'A GREATER THAN OR EQUAL TO D AND NOT C' 8 T; 'A = B OR C OR D' 9 T; 'A = B OR K = C OR 3' 10 T (the restated subject K inserted). Refusal half: a2 'A > B AND NOT GREATER THAN OR EQUAL TO C' (NOT before GREATER joins the operator, giving no 1985 operator) -> COBOL0001 refused; a3 'A = 1 OR KC OR = 5' -> COBOL2552 (a condition-name condition ends the insertion). a4: subscripted subject 'E (1) = 1 OR 4' 1 T, subscripted object inside the sequence 2 T, an abbreviated sequence inside its own parentheses after a full relation 3 T. On the lead-in's 'no parentheses are used within such a consecutive sequence': in §1985:VI.6.3.2.3 and 6.3.4 'parentheses' are the condition's grouping parentheses (Table 1), so subscript and arithmetic parentheses do not end the sequence; the reader's acceptance of abr4/abr8 stands on that reading, which the section's own usage supports. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:VI.6.3.3 SR2  (6.3.3 Abbreviated Combined Relation Conditions)  the text is in SR2'; 'OK  §1985:VI.6.3.2.3  (6.3.2.3 Precedence of Logical Operators and the Use of Parentheses)  the text is in the clause'.
